entry.title: Daily Digest — Wednesday, June 10, 2026
entry.content:
Topics in the News

  • A magnitude 7.8 earthquake strikes the southern coast of Mindanao in the Philippines, leaving at least 45 people dead.
  • Protests erupt against a proposed tourism development project on the environmentally protected island of Sazan, Albania.
  • An explosion at a Ta'ang National Liberation Army base in Myanmar leaves 43 people dead.
  • In Twenty20 cricket, the Indian Premier League concludes with Royal Challengers Bengaluru defeating Gujarat Titans in the final.

Hacker News

  • Building an HTML-first site doubled our users overnight — A case study on how stripping away JS-heavy complexity and going back to plain HTML dramatically improved reach and performance. (discussion, 987 points)
  • German ruling declares Google liable for false answers in AI Overviews — A landmark decision holding that AI-generated search summaries are Google's own speech, opening the door to defamation and accuracy liability. (discussion, 962 points)
  • I'm Eric Ries, author of "The Lean Startup" and new book "Incorruptible" – AMA — Live AMA with Eric Ries covering his new book on institutional reform alongside ongoing Lean Startup topics. (discussion, 515 points)
  • Mercedes-Benz starts large-scale production of electric axial flux motor — Mercedes begins mass-producing its in-house axial flux motors, which are significantly lighter and more power-dense than conventional radial designs. (discussion, 509 points)
  • πFS — A joke filesystem where all data is "stored" in the digits of pi — because any finite sequence of bits appears somewhere in pi, storage is theoretically free. (discussion, 492 points)
  • AWS Bedrock to require sharing data with Anthropic for Mythos and future models — AWS enterprise customers using Bedrock will have inference data shared with Anthropic as a condition of accessing next-generation models, raising privacy concerns. (discussion, 395 points)
  • Farmer donates land for a park, city sells it for $10M as data center land — A city quietly converted a charitable land donation meant for public parkland into a $10M data center sale, netting an expected $30M in future tax revenue. (discussion, 392 points)
  • Chrome is looking to permanently drop MV2 extensions — Google is moving to permanently retire Manifest V2, effectively killing uBlock Origin and similar content blockers, with Edge and Opera expected to follow. (discussion, 383 points)

LessWrong

  • Sequent: scale and automation for higher confidence in alignment by Geoffrey Irving — Introduces Sequent, a framework using scalable automated methods to build higher-confidence guarantees in AI alignment. (180 karma)
  • Even "illegible" Mythos reasoning traces seem pretty legible by faul_sname — Argues that Anthropic's Mythos model reasoning traces, despite being labeled opaque, are actually fairly interpretable on inspection. (111 karma)
  • Machinic Psychopharmacology: Do LLMs Self-Medicate? by Sid Black — Explores whether LLMs exhibit behavior analogous to self-medication when given tools or context that modulate their outputs. (98 karma)
  • Estimating No-CoT Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models by Anders Cairns Woodruff — Empirical estimates of how long frontier models can sustain reliable task completion without chain-of-thought prompting. (92 karma)
  • The Three Filters: Why Almost Every Plan to Survive ASI Fails Miserably by Alex Amadori — Proposes three evaluative filters that expose fatal flaws in most proposed strategies for navigating the transition to superintelligence. (69 karma)
